_steward_hook: Records this worktree, then prints the board. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-04-steward-coordination-design.md
🔴 `worktree 2>&1 1>/dev/null` IS DELIBERATE AND THE ORDER MATTERS. stderr carries the
NOTICES (HEAD moved here since the last session; another session was last seen here), which
are the entire point of the marker. stdout carries only the canonical scope, which exists for
scripting and which `who` prints on the next line anyway. `2>&1` first duplicates stderr onto
the terminal, THEN `1>/dev/null` silences stdout. Writing `>/dev/null 2>&1` instead throws the
notices away and leaves a hook that does nothing visible.
⚠ Both commands fail open and the whole thing is `|| true`: a session must never fail to start
because the steward was unreachable. 5s timeout covers two ~0.4s round trips.
A linked worktree usually has no backend/node_modules (10 of 17 on 2026-09-23), and this hook used to
require it and skip SILENTLY: no board, no worktree marker, so no HEAD-MOVED notice could ever fire.
It now runs through backend/scripts/lib/main-checkout-fallback.mjs, which borrows the MAIN checkout's
node_modules and .env; `$p` is left unquoted on purpose so it expands to two words or none. With no
node_modules anywhere it prints one 'skipped' line instead of nothing.

hooks.command: m="$(git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)/../backend"; if [ -d backend/node_modules ] || [ -d "$m/node_modules" ]; then p=; [ -f backend/scripts/lib/main-checkout-fallback.mjs ] && p="--import ./backend/scripts/lib/main-checkout-fallback.mjs"; node $p backend/scripts/steward.mjs worktree 2>&1 1>/dev/null; node $p backend/scripts/steward.mjs who 2>&1; else echo "steward: board skipped -- no backend/node_modules here or in the main checkout"; fi; true
